questions.text: Does the plan include specific measurable criteria to evaluate the success of its proposed actions?
questions.answer: The local government policy does include specific measurable criteria to evaluate the success of its proposed actions. The policy outlines a clear set of criteria for acceptable responses to climate change risks. These criteria include reducing risk to defined acceptable levels for an estimated time period, designing responses to be durable and effective for the estimated time period, and having reasonably well-known maintenance and operating costs. The policy also requires that responses should not adversely affect other properties, allow practical emergency response to events that exceed design risk, and identify the financial and operational capacity to meet any ongoing maintenance or operating costs. Furthermore, the policy stipulates that responses should allow for the continued viability of valued coastal ecosystems where these have been identified and where their continued viability is achievable at a cost acceptable to the wider community. These criteria provide a clear and measurable framework for evaluating the success of the policy's proposed actions.

questions.text: Does the document describe plans to conduct research in the local community, to inform climate actions?
questions.answer: The documents indeed describe plans to conduct research in the local community to inform climate actions. The local government has initiated a project to assess climate change risks on coastal areas. This project includes an investigation of community attitudes at the beginning, consultation with community groups, institutions, and state government agencies on their awareness and response to climate change issues. The project also includes a review of the literature covering experience with similar issues elsewhere, and an assessment of localities and infrastructure within the city which may be vulnerable to coastal hazards due to climate change. The project also plans to investigate adaptive management options in response to present and future coastal hazards. Finally, the project includes the preparation and execution of a communication plan to inform the community of the findings and initiate discussion about the preferred response.
